t: The British Crown took over the African Company of Merchants' nine forts in 1821; the Bond of 1844, by which Fante and other chiefs submitted murder and robbery to British jurisdiction, laid the legal basis of the colony proclaimed on 24 July 1874.
British rule was imposed on Asante by war: Kumasi was burnt in 1874, occupied again in 1896 when the asantehene was exiled, and annexed as a colony in 1902 after the War of the Golden Stool.
Cacao trees introduced in 1878 became the colony's mainstay; by the end of the 1940s the Gold Coast exported more than half of the world's cocoa, grown largely by African farmers.
dyk: Kwame Nkrumah won his seat in the Legislative Assembly election of February 1951 while in jail for sedition; the governor, Sir Charles Arden-Clarke, released him and invited him to form a government as 'leader of government business'.
ev: The British Crown dissolves the African Company of Merchants and places its Gold Coast forts under Charles MacCarthy, governor of Sierra Leone.
MacCarthy is killed and most of his force wiped out in a battle with Asante forces; a British, Fante and Accra force defeats an Asante invasion of the coast in 1826.
Commander Henry Worsley Hill negotiates the Bond of 1844 with Fante and other chiefs, who submit murder and robbery to British jurisdiction.
Sir Garnet Wolseley's force occupies and burns Kumasi in January; the coastal protectorate is proclaimed the Gold Coast Colony on 24 July.
A second British expedition occupies Kumasi, makes Asante a protectorate and exiles the asantehene.
After the War of the Golden Stool of 1900 Asante is proclaimed a colony and the Northern Territories a protectorate under the governor of the Gold Coast.
Rioting in Accra and other towns over ex-servicemen's pensions, housing and the foreign hold on the economy; Nkrumah and the UGCC's 'Big Six' are detained.
On 6 March the Colony of the Gold Coast becomes independent as Ghana.

f.capital: Cape Coast (Cape Coast Castle), then Christiansborg Castle at Accra after 1874
f.founder: Sir Charles MacCarthy, governor of Sierra Leone, given authority over the British forts in 1821; Commander Henry Worsley Hill, first governor of the Gold Coast (1843)
f.predecessor: The nine forts of the African Company of Merchants; the Fante and Ga coastal states; the Asante Empire; the Dutch and Danish Gold Coast
